description:
Start an Electron project from its source folder with the Chrome DevTools port open, then connect to its windows. No change to the app is needed.
PURPOSE: Zero-config desktop debugging. After it returns, the windows are connected as chromium targets: get_screen_state, screenshot, tap, input_text, logs, network and component inspection work on them.
HOW: electron-vite projects run `electron-vite dev --remoteDebuggingPort <port>`, others `electron . --remote-debugging-port=<port>`, using the project's own installed binary.
SAFETY: only a source folder is launched, so the app runs unpackaged. A packaged .app is refused: a CDP port on a packaged build lets anything that reaches it run code in the app.
GOOD: electron_launch_app({ projectPath: "~/code/myapp/apps/desktop" })
An app that pins its own port with appendSwitch('remote-debugging-port') is followed to that port (read from Chromium's startup line).
LIMITATIONS: Electron Forge and custom dev scripts are not detected.

port.description: CDP port to open (default 9222). Must be free.

projectPath.description: The Electron project's source folder (the one with package.json). A leading ~ is expanded.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the first window (default 60000; electron-vite compiles first).

name: electron_launch_app
